{{also|Appendix:Variations of "boy"}} ==Translingual== ===Etymology=== {{clip|mul|en:'''Bo'''do}} with {{m|mul|y}} as a placeholder. ===Symbol=== {{mul-symbol}} # {{ISO 639|3}} ===See also=== * {{langcat}} ==English== {{wp}} [[Image:School pupil of Darumawang El. school (7414531682).jpg|thumb|A '''boy''' (sense 1) wearing a backpack.]] ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|id=young male|:inh|enm:boye|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|boy//boye|t=servant, commoner, knave, boy}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*bōia|t=boy}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*bōjō}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*bōjô|t=younger brother, young male relation}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*bō-|t=brother, close male relation}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰā-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*bʰāt-|t=father, elder brother, brother}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|boy|t=boy}}, {{cog|fy|boai|t=boy}}, {{cog|nl|boi|t=boy}}, {{cog|nds|Boi|t=boy}}, and probably to the {{cog|ang|-}} proper name {{m|ang|Bōia}}. Also related to {{cog|stq|Bouge|t=boy}}, {{cog|vls|boe||brother}}, {{cog|no|-}} dialectal {{m|no|boa||brother}}, {{cog|nl|boef||rogue, knave}}, {{cog|bar|Bua|t=young boy, lad}}, {{cog|de|Bube}} {{gloss|"boy; knave; jack"; > English {{m|en|bub}}}}, {{cog|is|bófi||rogue, crook, bandit, knave}}, {{ cog|lmo|bagaj}} {{gl|"boy"; (< {{cog|gem|-}})}}. |passage=''B. Wooster:'' Of all the places on this great planet of ours, West Neck, Long Island, has chosen to be the most unexciting. The last time anything ''remotely'' interesting happened here was in 1842, when a '''tree''' fell over. They still talk about it in the village.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2019|month=October|author=Ian Walmsley|title=Cleaning up|journal=Modern Railways|page=42|text=When we see a train trapped behind (or embedded in) a fallen '''tree''' our first thought should be 'what was it doing there anyway?' {{...}}'''Trees''' are also responsible for numerous minor delays in autumn <small>[due to leaves falling on the track]</small>, which rolling stock engineers are supposed to cope with as usual.}}

#: {{ux|en|The banana '''tree''' is a tall perennial herb: its trunk is not woody.}}

#: {{ux|en|He had the choice of buying a scratching post or a cat '''tree'''.}}

# {{senseid|en|legislative body or building thereof}} {{lb|en|politics}} A building where a deliberative assembly meets; whence the assembly itself, particularly a component of a [[legislature]]. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}

# A [[dynasty]]; a family with its [[ancestor]]s and [[descendant]]s, especially a royal or noble one. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|A curse lay upon the '''House''' of Atreus.}}
# {{lb|en|metaphorical}} A place of [[rest]] or [[repose]]. {{defdate|from 9th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Jonson Every Man in His Humour|text=Like a pestilence, it doth infect / The '''houses''' of the brain.}}
#* {{RQ:Scott Lord of the Isles|text=Such hate was his, when his last breath / Renounced the peaceful '''house''' of death {{nb...}}.}}
# A [[grouping]] of [[schoolchildren]] for the purposes of competition in sports and other activities. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|I was a member of Spenser '''house''' when I was at school.}}
# An [[animal]]'s [[shelter]] or [[den]], or the shell of an animal such as a [[snail]], used for protection. {{defdate|from 10th c.}}
# {{lb|en|astrology}} One of the twelve divisions of an astrological chart. {{defdate|from 14th c.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=Religion and the Decline of Magic|passage=Since there was a limited number of planets, '''houses''' and signs of the zodiac, the astrologers tended to reduce human potentialities to a set of fixed types and to postulate only a limited number of possible variations.|year=1971|author=[[w:en:Keith Thomas (historian)|Sir Keith Vivian Thomas]]|page=313|isbn=978-0-14-013744-6|year_published=2012|publisher=[[w:en:Folio Society|The Folio Society]]}}
# {{lb|en|cartomancy}} The fourth [[Lenormand]] card.
# {{lb|en|chess|now|rare}} A [[square]] on a [[chessboard]], regarded as the proper place of a [[piece]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
# {{lb|en|curling}} The four [[concentric]] circles where points are scored on the [[ice]]. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
# [[lotto|Lotto]]; [[bingo]]. {{defdate|from 20th c.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} A [[child]]ren's [[game]] in which the players [[pretend]] to be members of a [[household]].
#: {{ux|en|As the babysitter, Emma always acted as the mother whenever the kids demanded to play '''house'''.}}
# {{lb|en|US|dialect}} A small [[stand]] of [[tree]]s in a [[swamp]].
# {{lb|en|sudoku}} A set of cells in a [[sudoku]] puzzle which must contain each digit exactly once, such as a row, column, or 3×3 box.
# {{lb|en|American football|slang|with “the”}} The [[end zone]].

# {{U|recently}} [[made]], or [[created]].
#: {{syn|en|brand new|recent|neo-|ceno-|Thesaurus:new}}
#: {{ant|en|ancient|dated|old}}
#: {{uxa|en|This is a '''new''' scratch on my car!   The band just released a '''new''' album.}}
#: {{ux|en|The cookers cost £350 '''new''' but £150 secondhand.}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=2007-01-30|author=Karen Crouse|title=Dash of Success Spices Up Gould’s Neighborhood|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2007/01/30/sports/football/30bears.html
|passage=Within a half-hour, Gould (pronounced GOLD) was stirring in pieces of breaded and sautéed chicken, pouring the finished sauce over fettucini noodles cooked al dente and serving one of the '''newest''' entrees from his growing recipe file — rustic chicken — to Tanner, his 9-year-old twin brothers, Colton and Austin, and their parents.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210211055414/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/01/30/sports/football/30bears.html}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=2007-05-24|author=David Pogue|title=How to Make Your Cellphone Act Like a BlackBerry|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2007/05/24/technology/24pogue.html
|passage=Only a few nonsmart models, primarily '''newer''' Razr models and a few Nokia phones, can run Yahoo Go. And once again, no Verizon phones need apply.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225192117/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/05/24/technology/24pogue.html}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-07-19|author=w:Timothy Garton Ash
|volume=189|issue=6|page=18|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|titleurl=http://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2013/jul/10/geopolitics-transatlantic-trade-deal|title=Where Dr Pangloss meets Machiavelli
|passage=Hidden behind thickets of acronyms and gorse bushes of detail, a '''new''' great game is under way across the globe. Some call it geoeconomics, but it's geopolitics too. The current power play consists of an extraordinary range of countries simultaneously sitting down to negotiate big free trade and investment agreements.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305122359/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2013/jul/10/geopolitics-transatlantic-trade-deal}}
## Of [[recent]] origin; having taken place [[recently]].
##: {{uxa|en|I can't see you for a while; the pain is still too '''new'''.   Did you see the '''new''' ''King Lear'' at the theatre?}}
# {{U|additional}}; recently [[discover]]ed.
#: {{syn|en|recent}}
#: {{ant|en|dated|old}}
#: {{uxa|en|We turned up some '''new''' evidence from the old files.}}
# {{U|current}} or [[later]], as opposed to [[former]].
#: {{syn|en|current}}
#: {{ant|en|former|old}}
#: {{uxa|en|My '''new''' car is much better than my previous one, even though it is older.   We had been in our '''new''' house for five years by then.}}
# Used to distinguish something established more recently, [[named after]] something or some place previously existing. <!-- shouldn't this be at [[New]]? -->
#: {{ant|en|old}}
#: {{uxa|en|'''New''' Bond Street is an extension of Bond Street.}}
# In [[original]] [[condition]]; [[pristine]]; not previously worn or used.
#: {{syn|en|brand new|brand [[spanking]] new|mint|pristine}}
#: {{ant|en|old|used|worn}}
#: {{uxa|en|Are you going to buy a '''new''' car or a second-hand one?}}
# [[refresh|Refreshed]], [[reinvigorate]]d, [[reform]]ed.
#: {{syn|en|born-again|reformed|refreshed|reinvigorated|revived}}
#: {{ant|en|old}}
#: {{uxa|en|That shirt is dirty. Go and put on a '''new''' one.   I feel like a '''new''' person after a good night's sleep.   After the accident, I saw the world with '''new''' eyes.}}
# [[newborn|Newborn]].
#: {{syn|en|newborn|young}}
#: {{ant|en|old}}
#: {{uxa|en|My sister has a '''new''' baby, and our mother is excited to finally have a grandchild.}}
# {{U|strange}}, [[unfamiliar]] or not previously [[know]]n.
#: {{syn|en|strange|unfamiliar}}
#: {{ant|en|familiar|old}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-07-06|volume=408|issue=8843|page=68
|title=The rise of smart beta
|url=http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21580518-terrible-name-interesting-trend-rise-smart-beta
|passage=Investors face a quandary. Cash offers a return of virtually zero in many developed countries; government-bond yields may have risen in recent weeks but they are still unattractive. Equities have suffered two big bear markets since 2000 and are wobbling again. It is hardly surprising that pension funds, insurers and endowments are searching for '''new''' sources of return.}}
#: {{uxa|en|The idea was '''new''' to me.   I need to meet '''new''' people.}}
# Recently [[arrive]]d or [[appear]]ed.
#: {{syn|en|novel|singular}}
#: {{ant|en|established}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=1|passage='Twas early June, the '''new''' grass was flourishing everywheres, the posies in the yard—peonies and such—in full bloom, the sun was shining, and the water of the bay was blue, with light green streaks where the shoal showed.}}
#: {{uxa|en|Have you met the '''new''' guy in town?   He is the '''new''' kid at school.}}
# [[inexperienced|Inexperienced]] or [[unaccustomed]] at some task.
#: {{syn|en|brand new|green}}
#: {{ant|en|accustomed|experienced|expert}}
#: {{uxa|en|Don't worry that you're '''new''' at this job; you'll get better with time.   I'm '''new''' at this business, I'm still '''new''' to the work.}}
# Of a [[period of time]], [[next]]; about to [[begin]] or recently [[begun]].
#: {{uxa|en|We expect to grow at 10% annually in the '''new''' decade.}}
